ideas.risks: The finite-bag generalization may be circular because the generated bag depends on hidden clean samples that are being enumerated. It may collapse back to the same dual-VC or tuple-enumeration bottleneck already identified.
ideas.summary: Ask an explorer to restate the da Cunha-Hogsgaard-Paudice route using only the finite set of hypotheses actually generated by polynomially many weak calls, rather than global assumptions on Range(A). The target is a precise conditional theorem: if hidden-clean weak-call distributions can be generated or sampled without enumeration, then finite-list validation handles the final classifier and no global VC(H) assumption is needed.
ideas.title: Finite-Bag da Cunha Theorem
ideas.why_promising: The solver attempt identifies controlled Range(A), dual VC, and final selector assumptions as the main gap. Some of these may be artifacts of proving uniform guarantees over an enormous output class, while the atlas learner only needs one validated finite final list.

ideas.risks: A positive lemma may be false for logarithmic witness size, giving only quasi-polynomial search. A negative result may only show failure of current proof skeletons, not of all boosters.
ideas.summary: Investigate whether the hidden clean tuples enumerated in residual-free boosting admit a polynomial hitting set under natural stability, compression, or bounded-randomness assumptions on the weak learner. The concrete deliverable is either a sampler that finds a successful clean transcript with inverse-polynomial probability, or a lower-bound example where every successful transcript has exponentially small raw-sample discovery probability.
ideas.title: De-enumerate Clean Transcripts
ideas.why_promising: This targets the exact algorithmic obstruction: clean conditional learning plus validation is enough, but blind enumeration of clean weak samples is too expensive. A hitting-set or anti-hitting-set theorem would be immediately useful.

ideas.risks: The model may remain too artificial to imply an atlas separation. Public constants, spike queries, artificial relabelings, and other concepts can still evade a hidden-target-noise argument.
ideas.summary: Formalize the adaptive public-filter information lemma in the random classification noise toy model. Include the selected filter in the transcript, charge raw samples and oracle outputs as mutual information about the hidden target, use the corrected KL transfer, and explicitly route low-OPT queries into hidden-target, public-witness, empirical/spike, and other-witness cases.
ideas.title: Adaptive Public-Filter Barrier
ideas.why_promising: The solver attempt has a clean algebraic identity showing that target-preserving filters beat the weak threshold only by correlating with the hidden target. Turning this into a rigorous adaptive toy theorem would clarify which positive strategies must leak target information.

ideas.risks: The resulting statement may only rule out very local residual methods. Sign-specific cells already refute overly broad global-correlation no-go claims, so the quantifiers must be exact.
ideas.summary: Solve the minimax problem for one-step observable filters and relabelings based on a current predictor g and sample (X,Y). Model the four cells of correctness of c and g, allow weights and labels depending on observable values such as (Y,g(X)) and signs, and determine whether positive excess err(g)-err(c)>epsilon ever guarantees a query with c-error below gamma.
ideas.title: Observable Relabeling Minimax
ideas.why_promising: Residual forcing from high-loss and mistake sets is known false, but the strongest possible one-step observable transformation has not been classified. A complete finite-dimensional obstruction would prevent future proofs from repeatedly rediscovering variants of the same failed idea.

ideas.risks: Known parity, code, CSP, PRF, and halfspace templates have already failed in broad form. The weak learner may become hard in exactly the low-noise regime needed, or strong improper learning may be possible by validation or list decoding.
ideas.summary: Search specifically for a represented class with an efficient fixed-slack learner below a low-noise threshold gamma, but conditional hardness of recovery under RCN noise eta>gamma. Focus on list-decodable code families, planted CSP-style classes, or SQ-hard classes where low-noise weak advantage is algorithmically easy but eta+epsilon recovery is conjecturally hard.
ideas.title: Threshold-Gap Separation Candidate
ideas.why_promising: RCN recovery converts strong agnostic learning into learning the hidden comparator. A genuine class with easy low-noise weak learning and hard moderate-noise recovery would give the negative route the run is still missing.

ideas.risks: Pathological weak learners can encode arbitrary bits in their outputs, so a theorem for arbitrary A is probably false. The right result may need to construct a new canonical weak learner, which the source assumption may not provide.
ideas.summary: Examine whether an arbitrary efficient improper fixed-slack learner can be transformed into a controlled-output learner without losing the weak guarantee. Try sample splitting, canonical empirical tie-breaking, output compression, or validation-based pruning; in parallel, build an adversarial weak learner that satisfies OPT+beta while forcing enormous dual VC or unstable outputs.
ideas.title: Regularize the Weak Learner
ideas.why_promising: The conditional da Cunha theorem becomes much closer to an atlas proof if Range(A), stability, or compression can be imposed without extra assumptions. If impossible, an explicit poisoning construction sharpens why controlled range is genuinely additional.
